name: Snapchatmaxxing

lead: Snapchatmaxxing is a community term for tuning one's presence on Snapchat so that photos and snaps present the user as favourably as possible. In practice that covers picking flattering angles and lighting, using lenses or filters, and keeping a profile that supports a first impression before any meeting.

The appeal is that the app is where many people first see each other. Forum users describe moving conversations to Snapchat, exchanging photos and then arranging meetings. No published study has tested the tactic itself, though researchers have studied filters and self-image more broadly.

paras: Users describe adding contacts from their local area, exchanging pictures and using the app as the step between a first message and a meet-up. Related habits include consistent lighting, camera angle choice and selective use of lenses. Forum posts treat it as a complement to other looks work, not a replacement.

Filtered or edited images can differ from how someone looks in person, which can lead to mismatched expectations at a meeting. Clinicians and researchers have described 'Snapchat dysmorphia', where people bring filtered selfies to cosmetic consultations, and some research links photo editing to body dissatisfaction. Privacy and image-sharing considerations apply, as with any messaging app.

chain: Choose flattering lighting, angle and lens
Photos present the user at their best
Stronger first impression with matches and contacts
angle.text: Practitioners use it to improve how they come across in images that precede an in-person meeting. It acts on presentation rather than on the face or body itself.

lead: Snapchatmaxxing is a term from looksmaxxing forums for optimising one's appearance and presentation on Snapchat, mainly to make a strong impression with people met online. It sits among the style and presentation 'metas' that concern how a person looks in images rather than in the mirror.[1]

Forum posts describe a pipeline in which contacts are added on the app, photos are exchanged and a meeting is then arranged; one user's thread declares the approach 'the key'.[1] Because first impressions on the app are formed from photos, proponents treat image quality, angle, lighting and lens choice as part of looks work.

No clinical research has examined the practice as such. Related literature covers filtered selfies and cosmetic-surgery interest, where the term 'Snapchat dysmorphia' was coined around 2018 by the British surgeon Tijion Esho.[2]

paras: The term follows the '-maxxing' naming pattern of the community, meaning to push a variable to its best achievable level. Here the variable is the image presented on social apps: photo selection, camera angle, lighting, lenses and filters.[1]
Community members describe it as a dating-market tactic, in which the app serves as the stage between a first message and meeting in person.[1]

Threads on looksmax.org mention the approach in connection with arranging dates, and discussion is often mixed with community slang about dating.[1] Related discussion concerns whether filters create expectations the person cannot meet in person.

Filters and edited selfies have drawn attention from clinicians. Wikipedia reports that surgeons began seeing patients who brought filtered selfies to consultations, and that a 2022 survey of facial plastic surgeons found most had patients wanting to look better in selfies.[2]

No studies found on snapchatmaxxing itself. Studies of the wider topic report links between photo editing and body dissatisfaction in adolescent girls, and between image-heavy social media use and openness to cosmetic surgery, as summarised in the Wikipedia article on Snapchat dysmorphia.[2]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the term appears in dating threads where users describe using Snapchat to meet people.[1]

claims.claim: "Snapchatmaxxing is the key" to setting up dates

timeline.event: Surgeon Tijion Esho coins 'Snapchat dysmorphia' after patients bring filtered selfies to consultations.[2]
Instagram bans filters that promote cosmetic surgery.[2]
